findings.title: Invalid flusher process counts are silently accepted
findings.body: SpanFlusher does not validate max_processes. An explicit 0 is converted by `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` into one process per shard, silently ignoring the configured limit and potentially spawning far more processes than intended. A negative value produces `num_processes <= 0`, an empty process-to-shards map, and therefore no flusher processes at all; submit() then finds no unhealthy processes to report while spans continue to be committed after being written to Redis but are never flushed. The CLI option in sentry.consumers accepts any integer, so this invalid configuration is reachable via --flusher-processes.

findings.title: Restarted flusher is started without waiting for the old process to exit
findings.body: When a process is unhealthy, _ensure_processes_alive() calls process.kill() but never join()s it before _create_process_for_shards() immediately starts a replacement for the same shards and overwrites self.processes[process_index]. kill() only signals termination, so the old and new flushers can briefly run concurrently against the same Redis shards, racing flush_segments()/done_flush_segments() and potentially producing the same segment twice to Kafka. The lost handle also prevents the caller from later confirming or reaping that specific child. The replacement should be started only after the killed process has been joined/reaped.

findings.title: Comma-joined shard metric tag corrupts multi-shard tags
findings.body: When one process handles multiple shards, shard_tag is built as a comma-joined string such as '0,2' and emitted as a single metrics tag value (also for segment_size_bytes and wait_produce). Comma is the separator between tags in StatsD/DogStatsD-style encoding, so the backend can parse this as an extra valueless tag instead of one shard tag, breaking per-shard filtering and creating malformed tag sets. The wait_produce metric also inconsistently uses the key 'shards' while the others use 'shard'. Metrics should be emitted per shard or use a separator that is valid in a single tag value.

findings.title: New multi-flusher test never verifies flushing or the spawn path
findings.body: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts process counts and shard-map totals, then joins; it never submits a span and never asserts that a process shared by multiple shards actually flushes a segment for each of its shards. All consumer tests also pass produce_to_pipe, which forces SpanFlusher into its threading.Thread branch, so the production spawn branch (run_with_initialized_sentry, pickling the per-shard SpansBuffer, and the new shards argument to SpanFlusher.main) is not exercised at all. A regression that breaks spawned flushers or drops all but one shard in a shared process would pass the new tests.
